---
applyTo:
  - ".github/workflows/**"
  - ".github/actions/**"
  - "Dockerfile"
  - "release/**"
  - "sonar-project.properties"
---

`AGENTS.md` is the root contract. This file specializes workflows, release automation, container build files, and Sonar config.

# Workflow And Release Rules

- Use minimal GitHub token permissions at the workflow or job level. Only grant elevated scopes to the job that needs them.
- External GitHub actions in modified files must pin the exact upstream commit SHA. Do not use floating branch refs such as `main`, `master`, or `trunk`, and do not rely on mutable release tags alone.
- When updating an external action reference, resolve the chosen stable upstream release tag to its full 40-character commit SHA at the time of the change. Keep the originating tag in an inline comment when practical so upgrades stay auditable.
- Verify action usage against the action's current official documentation when changing its major or minor release line. Preserve documented step ordering and supported inputs.
- ORAS setup jobs in workflows must stay on a node24-capable `oras-project/setup-oras` release line and request an ORAS CLI version that the pinned action release explicitly supports.
- ORAS publish commands in release scripts must avoid absolute on-disk layer paths unless path validation is intentionally disabled; prefer running from the asset directory and pushing relative artifact names.
- Helm OCI publication defaults must target the owner-qualified GHCR namespace derived from the active GitHub repository. If a non-GitHub registry layout is needed, override it explicitly with `HELM_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE` rather than relying on an incomplete default path.
- Revaer's default public Helm OCI repository is `oci://ghcr.io/<owner>/charts/revaer`. Keep workflow defaults, install docs, and Artifact Hub registration aligned to that owner-scoped path.
- The shipped `charts/revaer/artifacthub-repo.yml` template is the source of truth for the Artifact Hub repository ID. Release packaging may append ownership data, but it must not duplicate an existing `repositoryID`.
- Trivy SARIF uploads from the reusable image workflow must set an explicit `upload-sarif` category when workflow refactors would otherwise rename the analysis identity. Keep that category aligned with the legacy `ci.yml` build-image matrix key so GitHub code scanning can compare PR scans against `main`.
- Release packaging must preserve Artifact Hub ownership metadata when `ARTIFACTHUB_OWNER_NAME` and `ARTIFACTHUB_OWNER_EMAIL` are provided, even for unsigned packaging paths, because Artifact Hub ownership claim and verified-publisher flows depend on that published owner identity.
- Release packaging should publish an explicit `artifacthub.io/images` chart annotation for the Revaer image so Artifact Hub can index the runtime image and generate package security scans reliably.
- Helm packaging scripts must render multi-line chart annotations through quoted shell-safe file rendering instead of passing multi-line values through `awk -v`, because awk newline handling differs across local and CI environments.
- Workflows that install Rust toolchains must use the repository's configured toolchain source of truth rather than hard-coded ad hoc channels unless a documented exception is required. The shared setup action must reject a repository Actions toolchain variable that differs from `rust-toolchain.toml`; allowing rustup to silently install both versions is prohibited.
- Workflow build, lint, test, coverage, and release gates must call `just` recipes. Do not reintroduce raw `cargo` pipelines into CI jobs.
- `pr.yml` is the sole pull-request validation workflow. Keep formatting, lint, test, audit, deny, coverage, E2E, and other verification gates there so pull requests are validated exactly once before merge.
- `pr.yml` must run its release-build validation job on pull requests. Keep post-merge and tag publication in `ci.yml`, but do not hide PR release-build validation behind main/tag-only guards.
- Required CI recipes must install Rust CLI tools at exact reviewed versions with `--locked`; do not let floating registry resolution decide the tool version at check time. `just sqlx-install` must install SQLx CLI `0.8.6` because newer CLI releases can outrun the configured Rust toolchain, `just trunk-install` must install Trunk `0.21.14` because newer transitive CSS tooling can outrun the configured Rust toolchain, and `just udeps` must run cargo-udeps on the configured nightly toolchain directly because cargo-udeps requires nightly-only compiler flags.
- First-wave PR prerequisite jobs that gate downstream fan-out, including `instruction-drift`, `fmt`, `lint`, `check`, `helm-lint`, and `supply-chain`, must pass `cargo-cache: "false"` to `./.github/actions/setup-revaer` so required checks start their own Justfile gates instead of waiting on the multi-GB shared Cargo/sccache artifact restore. `lint`, `check`, `helm-lint`, and `supply-chain` must not request the native apt profile; native package setup belongs in native execution, coverage, media fixture, and image jobs that actually require it.
- `pr.yml` must run Rust and npm supply-chain checks through one combined `supply-chain` job that skips the shared Cargo/sccache artifact cache, restores version-keyed installed-tool caches, restores the Cargo advisory database cache, installs `cargo-audit`, `cargo-deny`, and `cargo-udeps` through the pinned prebuilt installer action, and then calls `just audit`, `just deny`, and `just udeps`. `just audit` must reject every advisory severity in both npm lockfiles as well as every Cargo advisory warning. Keep downstream jobs gated on `supply-chain`; do not split those checks back into separate setup-heavy jobs unless a new ADR records the timing evidence.
- The PR coverage job may reclaim unused GitHub-hosted runner toolchains after setup and migrations but before `just cov` so the workspace LLVM coverage run has enough disk. Keep the coverage command itself in `just cov`; the cleanup is runner preparation, not an alternate coverage gate.
- Sonar scan jobs must run from a clean full checkout, install the complete pinned Rust component set `rustfmt,clippy,llvm-tools-preview` before Sonar invokes Clippy, install `libtorrent-rasterbar-dev` so CFamily can resolve the system headers referenced by the native compile database, validate and fetch the pull request base branch before scanning, download only the prepared `coverage/lcov.info`, `coverage/js-lcov.info`, `coverage/compile_commands.json`, `coverage/cxxbridge/include/rust/cxx.h`, and `coverage/cxxbridge/include/revaer-torrent-libt/src/ffi/bridge.rs.h` inputs, keep Rust Clippy integration enabled with `sonar.rust.clippy.enabled=true`, keep Rust LCOV import enabled through `sonar.rust.lcov.reportPaths`, and keep JavaScript/TypeScript LCOV import enabled through `sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths`. `just cov` must exercise the complete workspace with all features and enforce the per-package line floor; JS/TS coverage must come from executed Node/Playwright/release code; both producer and consumer jobs must reject LCOV without real source and line-data records. Generate the native compile database and staged CXX headers before scanning, enable the generic YAML and JSON IaC analyzer with `sonar.featureflag.cloud-security-enable-generic-yaml-and-json-analyzer=true`, keep `sonar.yaml.activate=true` and `sonar.json.activate=true`, leave `sonar.kubernetes.file.suffixes` unset, assign every tracked Helm template manifest exactly through `sonar.lang.patterns.kubernetes`, and assign every other tracked YAML file exactly through the disjoint `sonar.lang.patterns.yaml`. This exact ownership must remain derived and enforced by `scripts/workflow-guardrails.sh` so no tracked YAML file is unclassified or multiply classified. Disable SCM-ignore exclusions with `sonar.scm.exclusions.disabled=true`, keep SCM analysis enabled with `sonar.scm.disabled=false` and `sonar.scm.provider=git`, enable project sensor-cache support so cross-file incremental symbolic execution is available, keep path, issue, coverage, duplication, JavaScript analyzer, SCA, and binary suffix exclusion properties absent or explicitly empty, keep JavaScript bundle detection disabled so committed bundles are analyzed, keep SCA dependency resolution strict, enable CFamily SCA and committed SPDX import, explicitly enable hidden-file and repository-wide text/secrets scanning, keep `sonar.plsql.file.suffixes=.plsql` so PostgreSQL `.sql` migrations are not misclassified as Oracle PL/SQL, keep `sonar.plsql.defaultSchema=public` for any actual PL/SQL analysis, wait for the quality gate, and fail before the scan if any Sonar input is missing or empty. The native compile database recipe must clean only the isolated `target/sonar-build` package before building so Cargo cannot skip the build script that writes `coverage/compile_commands.json` and stages the CXX bridge headers needed by CFamily analysis. Binary assets are not permission to exclude source paths, suffixes, or analyzer capabilities; any such exclusion requires explicit operator consent.
- `ci.yml` is the post-merge and tag-release workflow. Limit it to release-artifact, publish, and image-build activity for `main` pushes and release tags; do not duplicate PR validation jobs there.
- Manual release verification belongs in dedicated `workflow_dispatch` workflows, not in `pr.yml`, and should reuse the same `just` entrypoints and pinned third-party actions as the release path they exercise.
- Manual workflows that publish PR-scoped dev Helm artifacts should encode the PR number into the default prerelease version so registry output is traceable back to the reviewed change.
- `workflow_dispatch` string inputs that flow into shell or release commands must be validated and normalized before use. Reject unsafe or malformed values instead of passing them through to `just`, Helm, or release scripts.
- Reusable image workflows may publish PR-scoped dev Helm charts only as an optional post-manifest job. Keep that publish step downstream of the multi-arch manifest job, drive it through `just helm-package` and `just helm-publish`, and derive the default prerelease chart version from the caller-provided PR number.
- Release-tag image publication in `ci.yml` must not depend on `release-dev` or any other `main`-only job. Split dev and tag image publishing into separate jobs when their prerequisites differ.
- Stable tag activity in `ci.yml` must exclude prerelease tags consistently at the job boundary, not only in downstream publish jobs. Do not let prerelease tags build stable release artifacts that the later jobs refuse to publish.
- Reusable-workflow caller jobs must not use `secrets: inherit` unless the callee truly requires repository secrets. Prefer the default GitHub token plus explicit job permissions, and pass named secrets only when the callee consumes them.
- Helm chart validation and publication must flow through `just helm-lint`, `just helm-package`, and `just helm-publish`. Do not add ad hoc packaging or registry-push shell blocks to workflows.
- Workflow jobs that invoke `just helm-lint` must install `just` first through `./.github/actions/setup-revaer`; do not assume the runner image already provides it. The PR `helm-lint` job must not request the native apt profile because Helm chart validation does not need libtorrent or sccache packages.
- PR UI E2E jobs may request the runner-provided Chrome channel, but `just ui-e2e` must still install the exact Playwright browser targets it can launch. When Chromium is requested, install both `chromium` and `chromium-headless-shell` with Playwright's dependency installer so a partial browser cache cannot lack the executable used in headless test runs. Keep CI video capture disabled unless Playwright's bundled ffmpeg is intentionally installed. Keep the PR workflow readiness wait long enough for cold Rust and Trunk setup to finish before the Playwright global setup declares the UI server unavailable.
- Coverage-instrumented UI E2E runs must keep the Playwright and c8 command paths rooted at the repository root after any TypeScript precompile step. Do not leave the recipe shell inside `tests/` before invoking coverage tools or writing LCOV output, because CI shards must resolve the same Node binaries and source-map paths locally and remotely.
- Required CI recipes must never install Rust CLI tools from a floating registry resolution. Every `cargo install` in a required path must use an exact reviewed version and `--locked`; UI serve, build, development, and E2E recipes must depend on the canonical `trunk-install` recipe so all runners execute Trunk `0.21.14` from its published lockfile. Test harnesses and subprocess setup code must consume that pre-provisioned binary and are forbidden from installing or resolving required tools independently. An upstream yanked transitive package is not permission to remove `--locked`, float the version, or bypass the gate; upgrade the pinned tool deliberately with task-recorded validation.
- `just lint` runs `scripts/workflow-guardrails.sh`, which rejects unpinned external action refs, direct `${{ inputs.* }}` interpolation inside `run:` blocks, absent or non-empty Sonar strictness overrides, analyzer-level scope narrowing, degraded SCA options, duplicate or unreviewed Sonar properties, and workflow-level scanner-property overrides. The exact Sonar property allowlist is mandatory: adding even a strict property requires reviewing its semantics and intentionally updating the allowlist in the same change. Keep repeated guardrail failure headings centralized through `report_failure` so enforcement diagnostics stay consistent and do not create Sonar duplication findings, and bind helper positional parameters to named locals before use so shell-analyzer intent stays explicit. Treat `scripts/workflow-guardrails.sh` and `scripts/policy-guardrails.sh` as first-party enforcement code: fix Sonar findings in those scripts directly and do not add suppressions or exclusions for guardrail code without explicit operator consent recorded in the task ADR.
- Guardrail scans must ignore tracked paths that have been deleted in the current diff before invoking `rg` or `grep`, so deleted files do not create diagnostic noise while the remaining authored files stay fully scanned.
- `just udeps` must run cargo-udeps directly on the configured nightly toolchain instead of probing stable first; the stable probe is known setup overhead because cargo-udeps requires nightly-only compiler flags.
- `just lint` runs `scripts/media-compliance-guardrails.sh`, which verifies the media runtime image keeps required redistributable media tools, including the separately packaged FFplay playback verifier, source-offer links, notices, inventory/SBOM labels, the ExifTool exception artifact, structured final-image compliance-bundle validation, package-level SPDX version/license/SHA-256 evidence, and the default-image `--enable-nonfree` ban aligned.
- `deny.toml` duplicate-crate tolerances must stay exact-version scoped, ADR-backed, and current with the lockfile. Remove unmatched or unnecessary skip entries when dependency upgrades make them stale.
- Cargo advisory findings and warnings are mandatory fixes. Keep `.secignore` empty, keep `deny.toml` advisory ignores empty, and keep `just audit` free of an ignore mechanism. Do not add an advisory exception without explicit operator consent recorded in the task ADR, a time-bounded expiry, and an intentional guardrail update in the same commit; convenience, transitive ownership, inactive features, or an upstream delay are not consent.
- npm advisory findings at every severity are mandatory fixes for both `tests/package-lock.json` and `release/package-lock.json`. Do not lower `--audit-level`, omit a lockfile, or add an npm audit exception without the same explicit operator consent, task ADR, expiry, and guardrail change required for Cargo exceptions.
- Media runtime image publication must remain disabled unless the reusable image workflow receives and validates an explicit final-image compliance bundle generated for the exact image build. `build-images.yml` must run `scripts/validate-final-image-compliance-bundle.sh` before any image login, push, manifest, signing, or Helm publication step, then stage the validated bundle into `release/media-compliance/final-image-compliance-bundle.json` so the Dockerfile copies that exact manifest into `/app/compliance/final-image-compliance-bundle.json`. Verification-only image builds may use the checked-in placeholder bundle, but published images must use the validated staged manifest. Do not pass `final_image_compliance_bundle` from `ci.yml` until release automation creates that final-image evidence before the first push.
- The shipped media runtime SPDX inventory must enumerate runtime packages individually, including Alpine package version, declared/concluded license, and SHA-256 package digest. Do not collapse runtime packages into aggregate `NOASSERTION` entries.
- PR image checks may run non-publishing image-build, scan, manifest-input, and Helm-packaging verification when the reusable image workflow does not receive a final-image compliance bundle. Those PR checks must not push images, create manifests, sign images, or publish Helm charts without the bundle gate.
- `pr.yml` must run its release-build validation job on pull requests. Keep post-merge and tag publication in `ci.yml`, but do not hide PR release-build validation behind main/tag-only guards.
- `pr.yml` must run the media conversion fixture gate on every PR. In stack layers that do not yet contain `crates/revaer-media-runtime/tests/media_fixtures.rs`, the job must write and publish an explicit not-applicable `target/media-conversion-report.md` instead of pretending the absent target was tested. Once that target exists, the gate must run through `just download-test-fixtures`, `just generate-test-fixtures`, `just verify-test-fixtures`, and `just test-media-conversion`, with ignored fixture binary directories restored from a cache keyed by the fixture manifest, scripts, and media tool versions. The media fixture job must pass `cargo-cache: "false"` to `./.github/actions/setup-revaer` so it does not block fixture execution on the multi-GB shared Cargo/sccache restore path. The gate must publish the generated report into the GitHub job summary and upload it as a workflow artifact so the media actions and outcomes are reviewable from one report.
- Runtime image contents copied from the builder must remain root-owned. Keep `/app`, `/app/docs`, `/app/config`, and `/app/compliance` root-owned; copy each `/app/compliance` file as root-owned read-only content; and leave runtime write access only on declared volumes plus the documented OpenAPI output directory `/app/docs/api`.
- Treat `sonar-project.properties` as the versioned source of truth for complete tracked-entry Sonar scope, SCM-ignore exclusion disabling, full SCM blame reload, enabled cross-file analyzer cache support, retained scanner-report evidence, strict empty scope-filter overrides, binary suffix exclusion prohibition, exact HTML and Kubernetes language suffix mapping, Rust LCOV import, JavaScript/TypeScript LCOV import, native compile database import, staged native CXX bridge header imports, JavaScript committed-asset analysis, generic YAML/JSON IaC analysis, SQL dialect suffix separation, SCA dependency-resolution strictness, CFamily SCA, committed SPDX import, and quality-gate waiting. `sonar.sources` must match every authored top-level entry returned by `git ls-files` and must not use `.` because that pulls the untracked `.git` object database into source indexing. `sonar.tests` must equal the committed empty `.sonar-test-scope` sentinel; no authored file may enter that directory or test-only scope. This deliberately disables Sonar's automatic path heuristic so files under `docs` and `tests` remain eligible for main-code rules and secrets analysis. Every PR and main scan must call `just sonar-verify-result` after scanner completion and retain the nonempty report-task metadata and complete submitted scanner report as an artifact; missing positive coverage metrics, ignored quality-gate conditions, unresolved new-code issues, or unreviewed new-code hotspots must fail the workflow.
- Sonar evidence archive verification must remain fail-closed and pipefail-safe. Do not verify scanner-report archives with a short-circuiting pipe such as `tar -tf ... | grep -q ...`; write the archive listing to an explicit file first and then search that file so broken-pipe behavior cannot convert valid evidence into a workflow failure.
- Sonar is a strict first-party quality gate. Do not add, broaden, or reintroduce Sonar issue ignores, rule-scope restrictions, source/test inclusions or exclusions, coverage exclusions, duplication exclusions, analyzer default exclusions, binary suffix exclusions, bundle/generated-code skips, disabled available analyzers, SCA exclusions, SCA no-resolve settings, manifest-failure tolerance, SCM disablement, SCM-ignore-based hiding, scanner skip switches, quality-gate relaxation, `NOSONAR`, or comparable suppressions without explicit operator consent recorded in the task ADR. Do not add authored first-party files to `sonar.exclusions`, `sonar.inclusions`, `sonar.test.exclusions`, `sonar.test.inclusions`, `sonar.coverage.exclusions`, `sonar.cpd.exclusions`, `sonar.javascript.exclusions`, `sonar.sca.exclusions`, binary suffix exclusion properties, `.sonar-test-scope`, or any test-only classification to make findings disappear; do not rely on `.gitignore`, analyzer default dependency-directory exclusions, generated-code detection, automatic test-path detection, or scanner defaults to hide files that should be fixed. Those scope-filter properties must stay explicitly empty or absent unless an operator explicitly approves a task-scoped exception. Assigning PostgreSQL files to the Oracle PL/SQL analyzer, weakening analyzer activation, or accepting scanner warnings as normal is Sonar criteria relaxation. Convenience, scanner noise, time pressure, generated-code discomfort, vendored-code discomfort, binary assets, duplication discomfort, coverage discomfort, dependency-resolution failures, a skipped scan, skipped entitled dependency analysis, missing coverage inputs, missing native analyzer inputs, disabled analyzer feature flags, missing SCM blame, deprecated analysis parameters, quality-of-analysis warnings, scanner `WARN` lines, or a desire to make CI pass are never valid reasons to relax Sonar. Fix the finding, add real coverage, supply the precise analyzer input, delete or regenerate the offending artifact, or stop and obtain explicit operator consent before weakening the gate. The agent MUST stop before editing any criterion and obtain a new operator statement naming the exact property, scope, reason, and expiry; an agent-authored ADR, silence, prior unrelated approval, inferred intent, or a request to make CI green is not consent.
- Do not add fake PL/SQL data-dictionary JDBC settings to silence or reduce warnings. Sonar's PL/SQL data-dictionary mode queries Oracle dictionary views and is only valid when a real Oracle dictionary is intentionally available. PostgreSQL `.sql`, `.pgsql`, and `.plpgsql` files must not be routed into that Oracle analyzer just to appear analyzed.
- Release-tooling dependency changes under `release/**`, including JavaScript lockfiles such as `release/package-lock.json`, must stay manifest-scoped, avoid unrelated workflow churn, and update this instruction file in the same change so instruction-drift remains explicit. A local replacement for an unused semantic-release plugin is acceptable only when `release/release.config.js` does not invoke that plugin and `npm --prefix release audit --audit-level=low` remains clean without audit exceptions.
- Prerelease Helm assets must be produced during the semantic-release prepare phase so the packaged chart version matches the dev release version exactly. OCI publication must consume those already-packaged assets after the GitHub release assets exist.
- Stable tag releases must package the Helm chart once, attach the `.tgz`, `.prov`, and public key to the GitHub release, and publish that exact packaged chart to the OCI registry. Avoid repackaging between release-asset upload and OCI publication.
- JavaScript release metadata helpers under `release/**` and coverage-only semantic-release helper scripts should stay side-effect scoped. Prefer ESM with top-level await for Node helper entrypoints that invoke async hooks, and prefer wiring shell packaging steps in the semantic-release `prepareCmd` over spawning child processes from Node glue unless a documented exception is required.
- Semantic-release command templates under `release/**` must remain lodash-template-safe. Do not embed shell parameter-expansion forms such as `${VAR:-default}` inside configured command strings because lodash templating parses the same `${...}` syntax first. Semantic-release placeholders such as `${nextRelease.version}` remain allowed; for shell conditionals prefer plain shell variable references such as `"$VAR"` or move the conditional logic into a script.
- Helm packaging scripts must exclude repository-level Artifact Hub metadata from the chart tarball itself. Publish `artifacthub-repo.yml` as a separate OCI artifact instead of shipping it inside the chart package.
- Helm publishing must verify signed chart artifacts before OCI push, and temporary exported secret keyring files must be created with owner-only permissions.

# Shell Safety

- Never interpolate untrusted `${{ inputs.* }}` or comparable expression values directly into `run:` blocks.
- Map user-controlled inputs into environment variables first, validate or whitelist them, then consume them in shell.
- When writing validated values to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, use the multiline heredoc form so output parsing stays safe even if the value surface changes later.
- Prefer arrays and quoted expansions over word-splitting command strings.
- Setup-action package-list inputs may accept general shell whitespace, including CRLF-pasted multiline input, when that improves YAML readability, but the resulting tokens must still be normalized into a validated array before invocation.

# Credentials And Test Infrastructure

- CI-only credentials may be ephemeral only when they are clearly scoped to isolated test infrastructure, such as throwaway Postgres service containers.
- Ephemeral test credentials must never be reused as application secrets, committed runtime credentials, or user-facing examples.
- Postgres service containers used by migration-heavy gates must request explicit shared memory aligned with local `just db-start` defaults; the current default is 1 GiB because Docker's default shared-memory segment and the previous 256 MiB setting are too small for parallel database test runs.
- `just db-start` must use explicit provenance instead of inferring ownership from `DATABASE_URL` presence alone. A caller that synthesized a local URL and expects Docker lifecycle ownership must pass `REVAER_DB_MANAGED=1`; an operator-supplied URL remains external by default, must be probed and honored when reachable, and must fail fast when unreachable. Managed mode is valid only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `host.docker.internal`. Keep `just validate`, `just cov`, and Playwright global setup aligned with this contract.
- Do not log secrets or secret-like values. Mask or omit them.
- Do not embed password-bearing database URI literals in workflows, the Justfile, release scripts, docs, or tests. Local and CI test database credentials may use explicit non-production defaults, but connection strings must be composed from variables or helper scripts so Sonar secret analysis has no inline password URI to report.
- Keep Helm registry credentials (`HELM_API_KEY_ID`, `HELM_API_KEY_SECRET`) separate from chart-signing material (`HELM_GPG_PRIVATE`, `HELM_GPG_PUBLIC`). Publishing jobs may use registry credentials only when consuming an already-packaged chart artifact.
- GHCR chart publication on GitHub-hosted runners should prefer the job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` plus explicit `packages: write` over long-lived custom registry secrets. Keep `HELM_API_KEY_*` only for non-GitHub or local override paths.

# Drift Control

- Any change to a workflow, release script, setup action, `justfile`, or `sonar-project.properties` must review the matching instruction file in the same change.
- Revaer enforces that rule mechanically with `just instruction-drift`, backed by `scripts/instruction-drift-check.sh`. Keep the mapping in that script aligned with this file and `AGENTS.md`.
- Keep `scripts/workflow-guardrails.sh` aligned with the live workflow policy when GitHub Actions pinning or shell-safety rules change.
- `pr.yml` must pass explicit base/head SHAs into `just instruction-drift` so pull requests are checked against the real reviewed diff, not an incidental worktree state.
- Drift coverage for actions and release assets is recursive. Changes under `.github/actions/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, and `release/**` must keep matching the devops instruction update rule.
- Reusable workflows that publish images must preserve `packages: write` on the caller job because the callee cannot elevate a more restrictive token.
- Reusable-workflow caller jobs must define one merged `permissions` map. Do not duplicate the `permissions` key in a job to append scopes later; GitHub Actions rejects the workflow before execution.
- Keep the Sonar PR gate blocking in both places: PR decoration/status and scanner execution. Do not remove `sonar.qualitygate.wait=true`, reduce the timeout, or weaken branch protection without explicit operator consent recorded in the task ADR.
